title: An AI-enabled structural atlas decodes kinase specificity across the human proteome - Nature Biotechnology
text:
AbstractOf the 1.8 million serine/threonine/tyrosine residues in the human proteome, only 6% bear experimental validation of phosphorylation, and only 5% of these have been mapped to a kinase. Here we present KinoPlex, a computational framework that integrates predicted protein structures and kinase recognition motifs to assign phosphorylation potential and kinase specificity to all serine/threonine/tyrosine residues. Using ~20,000 AlphaFold models and positive-unlabeled transfer learning, we identified ~567,000 residues as structurally phospho-competent. We intersected these with kinase position-specific scoring matrices to quantify motif specificity, yielding ~250,000 high-confidence candidates with sequence recognition potential and optimal structural presentation. The structural atlas uncovered fundamental organizing principles guiding kinase substrate recognition and dynamics of phosphorylation, including a phenomenon we call sequence–structure selective coupling, whereby kinases achieve specificity through structural scarcity of their preferred motif (negative-selecting kinases) or promiscuity through its structural accessibility (positive-selecting kinases), rather than by motif discrimination alone. Deep phosphoproteomics in K562 cells validates KinoPlex predictions and kinase enrichment capacities.

Data availability

The raw MS files are deposited in MassIVE under accession number MSV000099698 (ref. 67). Derived analysis tables are included as Supplementary Tables. An interactive portal for browsing the atlas is hosted by Cell Signaling Technology/PhosphoSitePlus at kinoplex.phosphosite.org. The entire structural atlas and whole-proteome PSSM percentiles are accessible at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20633591 (ref. 68).
Code availability

Our website and associated code are hosted by Cell Signaling Technologies on PhosphoSitePlus. The website can be found at kinoplex.phosphosite.org. The website uses Kinase Library-derived PSSMs for site scoring but scores sites against a proteome-wide background. Furthermore, we have code for extraction of structural features at https://github.com/dvanderwall/KinoPlex ref. 69. Proteome-wide kinase PSSM percentiles as well as the structural atlas are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20633591 (ref. 68).

Additional informationPublisher’s note Springer Nature remains neutral with regard to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations.Extended dataExtended Data Fig. 1 Structural distinctions between known and uncharacterized serine, threonine, and tyrosine (STY) residues across the human proteome.(a) AlphaFold Database Protein Structure Acquisition. AlphaFold v2 structures for >20,000 canonical human proteins were analyzed to systematically extract 3-Dimensional structural features for every serine, threonine, and tyrosine (STY) residue. The human proteome contains approximately 1.8 million STY residues, each assessed within its native predicted protein structure. Representative examples shown include Hexokinase, Arginine tRNA Ligase, Sestrin-1, and Albumin. (b) Exemplar Structural Feature Schematics. Half-sphere exposure (HSE) metrics quantify the spatial distribution of neighboring atoms within a 10 Å radius around the phospho-acceptor’s Cα or Cβ atom. This volume is partitioned into upper and lower hemispheres relative to the backbone orientation. Packing density is assessed using virtual spherical probes (radii 0.2-2.0 Å3) to estimate the volume accessible within local cavities defined by atomic coordinates within a 10 Å radius; a representative probe of 0.8 Å3 is depicted. Solvent accessibility is measured using rolling probes to calculate both total solvent-accessible surface area (SASA) and hydroxyl-specific accessibility (reflecting kinase access to the reactive group). Pocket geometry metrics include Cartesian dimensions (x, y, z), total volume, and local pocket depth and openness, calculated from atoms residing within a 10 Å shell. Non-covalent interactions including π–π stacking, side-chain hydrogen bonding, and backbone interactions are computed across the local residue environment, with angular and energetic parameters extracted. Biophysical microenvironment descriptors such as local hydrophobicity, polarity, and electrostatic potential are quantified both at the residue level and within the surrounding pocket. (c) Structural Features Carry Discriminative Power. Violin plots of representative structural features, including pLDDT, disorder score, 8 A packing density, Hydroxyl SASA, and among serines and threonines. Comparison of structural feature distributions between Known sites (blue, n = 100,880) and Uncharcterized sites (orange, n = 1,367,324), revealing systematic enrichment of phosphosites in disordered, solvent-accessible, and low-density regions. Boxplots within the violin are centered on the median surrounded by the interquartile range. The inner diamond reflects the mean. Box whiskers extend to 1.5*IQR. P-values were derived both by Mann-Whitney U test and Kruskal-Wallis H test with BH p-value adjustment; *** indicates p-value = 0. (d) Secondary Structure and Local Micro-Environments Contribute To Site Discrimination. Bar plots show the fraction of serine and threonine residues assigned to canonical secondary-structure classes (α-helix, 310-helix, β-strand, turn, bend, coil/unstructured) across the full structural atlas. Known sites (orange) are markedly enriched in unstructured conformations (two-sided Fisher’s exact, BH adj. p < .01) with a significant amount of alpha-helices (two-sided Fisher’s exact, BH adj. p < .01). Percent labels denote the proportion of sites per class. (e) Joint Density Analysis of Solvent Accessibility and Disorder Reveals Two Phosphorylation Regimes. Kernel density estimates (filled contours; labels denote relative density) depict the bivariate distribution of disorder score (x-axis) and total SASA (y-axis, Å2) for All Uncharacterized (Left) and All Known (Right) sites. The density plot is color scaled with the density measurement for that color annotated in the contours, yellow reflecting higher density and purple denoting lower density. Known sites concentrate predominantly in a high-disorder/high-accessibility basin, consistent with phosphorylation favoring flexible, solvent-exposed regions. A secondary cluster of Known sites with low disorder but high SASA is also evident, indicating a structured-yet-accessible mode wherein residues on well-exposed surfaces of ordered elements are permissive for phosphorylation. Uncharacterized sites show relative enrichment in low-disorder/low-accessibility regions. (f) Positive Unlabeled Classification Paradigm. Left: Assigning Training Labels. Approximately 116,000 serine, threonines, and tyrosines characterized by Ochoa et al., 2020 constitute the positive class (“Known” sites). All other ~1.7 million unannotated serine, threonine, and tyrosine (STY) constitute the negative class (“Uncharacterized” sites). Note that the negative class includes phospho-competent and phospho-incompetent sites which have not yet been annotated. Middle: Feature Extraction and Normalization. Each site is encoded as a high-dimensional feature vector derived from the KinoPlex structural library. Prior to separation of sites, feature scaling and centering is performed. Right: Defining Training and Testing Datasets. Training and testing datasets were defined independently for serines, threonines, and tyrosines in order to build three separate models. Among these residues, 80% were used as training and 20% of were used as testing, and the sampling ratio was maintained.Extended Data Fig. 2 Kinome-Wide PSSM Scoring Framework.(a) Global Kinase PSSM Scoring. All ~1.8 million STY residues were scored against ~300 kinase-specific PSSMs, yielding a kinase–site score matrix representing motif avidity across the phosphoproteome. For each kinase, the score distribution was bootstrapped using 100,000 randomly sampled sites to estimate quantiles and their associated 95% confidence intervals. (b) Exemplar Motif Score Distributions of Known (blue) and Uncharacterized (orange) Sites. The red vertical line denotes the bootstrapped 99th percentile threshold; sites to the right of this line exhibit high motif compatibility with at least one kinase. Known phosphosites were significantly enriched above this threshold relative to unannotated sites.Extended Data Fig. 3 Kinase Family and Per-Kinase Bootstrapped Structural Features.(a-c) Kinase Family-Specific Structural Signatures Revealed by Unsupervised Clustering. Boxplots depict the distribution of bootstrapped median structural feature score, with box spanning the interquartile range and whiskers extending to 1.5*IQR. For each kinase, all sites exceeding the kinase’s 99th percentile PSSM were treated as its substrate pool. Kinase-substrate annotations were used to construct a heatmap of eight major kinase groups. Each kinase was mapped to its family such that all of its associated substrates were annotated as belonging to the kinase’s parent family. Features were then extracted across all sites in the family, and means for each feature were bootstrapped (n = 500). Bootstrap feature means were also derived for all phospho-competent sites, all phospho-incompetent sites, and all sites to serve as controls. Across (a) pLDDT, (b) SASA, and (c) disorder score, we see significant inter-family divergence (see Supplementary Table 3). Sample sizes of families include AGC = 1635, Atypical = 715, CAMK = 1393, CK1 = 839, CMGC = 2445, Other = 1244, STE = 380, and TKL = 260. (d) Per-Kinase Distribution of Mean Disorder Score. For each kinase, we bootstrapped all median structural features (disorder score depicted here, n = 500). The bar height reflects the empirical median while error bars reflect the 95% CI of the resampled medians. Kinase name labels colored by family matching the phylogenetic tree. Bar height and color reflective of the disorder score. Kinase labels are colored by kinase family in accordance with the kinase phylogeny image in the center of the plot. (e) Proportion of Site Predictions At High-Scoring Kinase Thresholds. Fraction of sites that achieve ≥95th, ≥99th, or ≥99.9th percentile for at least one kinase PSSM score distribution when using the proteome-wide STY background as the null. Bars summarize three site classes: Known Sites, Sites Predicted Phospho-Competent, and Sites Predicted Phospho-Incompetent. Bar height reflects proportion of sites within each site class exceeding the PSSM percentile threshold for at least one kinase (n = 303 S/T-kinases).
